'''Marie Litzinger''' (May 14, 1899 – April 7, 1952) was an American mathematician known for her research in [[number theory]], [[homogeneous polynomial]]s, and [[modular arithmetic]].

== Early life and education ==
Marie Litzinger was born in [[Bedford, Pennsylvania]], the daughter of Rush Litzinger and Katherine O'Connell Litzinger.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|date=1948-06-17|title=Mrs. Katherine Litzinger|pages=2|work=Bedford Gazette|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/88545330/mrs-katherine-litzinger/|access-date=2021-11-08|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her father owned a marble works, and was an accountant for the [[Pennsylvania Railroad]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=1927-06-10|title=Bedford Loses Prominent Citizen|pages=1|work=Bedford Gazette|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/88545753/bedford-loses-prominent-citizen/|access-date=2021-11-08|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

Litzinger earned her [[bachelor's degree]] and [[master's degree]] at [[Bryn Mawr College]] in 1920<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bryn Mawr College. Senior Class|url=http://archive.org/details/brynmawrcollegey1920bryn|title=Bryn Mawr College Yearbook. Class of 1920|date=1920|publisher=Bryn Mawr, PA: Bryn Mawr College|others=Special Collections Bryn Mawr College Library}}</ref> and 1922, respectively. She won the college's European Fellowship in 1920.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1920-07-24|title=Miss Marie Litzinger|pages=8|work=Corsicana Daily Sun|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/88545197/miss-marie-litzinger/|access-date=2021-11-08|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She completed her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1934.<ref name="mathgeo">{{MathGenealogy|id=6319}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Edwards|first1=Harold M.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Eq5072shy9AC&dq=Marie+Litzinger&pg=PA182|title=A Century of Mathematics in America|last2=Duren|first2=W. L.|date=1988|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=978-0-8218-0130-7|pages=182|language=en}}</ref> Her doctoral advisor was [[Leonard Eugene Dickson]], one of the first American researchers in [[abstract algebra]].<ref name="mathgeo" /> Her dissertation was titled "A Basis for Residual Polynomials in ''n'' Variables."<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
While studying, Litzinger taught mathematics at secondary institutions, before becoming an instructor at [[Mount Holyoke College]] in 1925, where she remained for the rest of her career and rose to the rank of full professor in 1942.<ref name=":0" /> She also served as department chair. She was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]], among other professional societies.<ref name=":0">{{citation|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/litz.htm|title=Marie Litzinger|work=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|accessdate=2015-12-26|date=January 10, 2014|first=Larry|last=Riddle|publisher=Agnes Scott College}}.</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title = The Biographical Dictionary of Women in Science: L-Z|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=LTSYePZvSXYC|publisher = Taylor & Francis|date = 2000-01-01|isbn = 9780415920407|language = en|first1 = Marilyn Bailey|last1 = Ogilvie|first2 = Joy Dorothy|last2 = Harvey|author-link = Marilyn Bailey Ogilvie|author2-link = Joy Harvey}}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics |volume=34 |series=History of mathematics | first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2009 |isbn=9780821843765 |contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA230 |pages=230–231 |contribution=Litzinger, Marie, May 14, 1899–April 7, 1952}}. Biography on p.370-371 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

== Personal life ==
Litzinger died in her hometown, Bedford, Pennsylvania, in 1952, aged 52 years.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1952-04-18|title=Noted Teacher Dies in Bedford|pages=2|work=Everett Press|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/88545613/noted-teacher-dies-in-bedford/|access-date=2021-11-08|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

== Papers ==
The Marie P. Litzinger Papers, which consist of Litzinger's college correspondence and photographs, are held at Bryn Mawr College with the  Collection Identifier BMC-M124.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archives.tricolib.brynmawr.edu/repositories/6/resources/5777|title=Collection: Marie P. Litzinger Papers &#124; Archives & Manuscripts|website=archives.tricolib.brynmawr.edu}}</ref>
